subject: ophthalmology
title: Ocular injuries

steps.tx: **Chemical burns** are graded by limbal ischaemia and corneal clarity under the Roper Hall and Dua systems. **Alkalis** such as lime and ammonia saponify tissue and penetrate deeply, while **acids** coagulate protein and precipitate a barrier that limits depth. First aid is immediate copious irrigation with water or litres of saline, everting the lids and sweeping particles until pH testing reads neutrality before any history. Later care debates debridement, ascorbate, brief steroids with tetracyclines, amniotic membrane and stem cell transplantation for limbal failure, since symblepharon and dry eye scar late.
steps.say: A burnt eye must be irrigated with litres of fluid first, and questions come later. Alkali from lime or ammonia melts deeper than acid because it saponifies tissue, while acid coagulates protein into a barrier. Evert the lids, sweep out particles, and keep irrigating until the pH reads neutral. Grading by limbal whitening and corneal clarity then guides later care with steroids, amniotic membrane and stem cell grafting for limbal failure.

steps.tx: The photograph shows an eye after copious irrigation with the lids everted to expose trapped particles. A diffuse **corneal stromal haze** clouds the centre and signals stromal injury from the chemical, while **perilimbal whitening** rings the cornea and marks **limbal ischaemia** that grades severity. This pairing of haze with ischaemia defines a serious burn, so the priority stays immediate prolonged irrigation to neutrality before grading, debridement or grafting.
steps.say: Look at this eye and notice the lids held everted after copious irrigation, which exposes the fornices where particles hide. The centre of the cornea has a stromal haze that clouds the iris detail beneath. Around the edge, the perilimbal whitening marks limbal ischaemia, which is the grading sign that predicts healing. For the exam, link haze with stromal damage and whitening with limbal stem cell loss, and remember that irrigation to neutrality always comes first.

steps.tx: **Open globe** injury demands shielding without pressure, nil by mouth, tetanus cover, antiemetics, no drops and no manipulation of tissue. CT hunts foreign bodies before urgent repair closes wounds layer by layer, with lens and vitreous work staged second. **Berlin oedema** from commotio retinae whitens the retina and observes, while choroidal rupture draws crescent streaks and watches for new vessels. **Traumatic optic neuropathy** follows blunt trauma with a relative afferent pupil defect and an initially normal disc, and megadose steroid debates with canal decompression stay selected. Repair starts endophthalmitis prophylaxis.
steps.say: A cut eye must be shielded without pressure, starved, covered for tetanus, settled against vomiting, scanned by CT and sewn without delay. You must never press the globe, pull tissue back, or instil drops. Commotio retinae whitens the retina and is watched, while choroidal rupture streaks the fundus and is monitored for new vessels. Blunt trauma with a pupil defect but a normal disc suggests optic nerve injury, which keeps steroids and decompression as selected options.

steps.tx: **Hyphaema** layers blood in the anterior chamber after blunt trauma tears the iris root or ciliary vessels, and grading by height guides admission. Sickle cell trait or disease rebleeds catastrophically even at low pressure, so pressure control avoids carbonic anhydrase inhibitors in sickle patients. Management raises the head, shields the eye, adds cycloplegics with cautious steroids and pressure control, and watches for rebleed peaking around day five. Total black ball hyphaema threatens corneal staining, while **corneal blood staining** with yellow green discoloration needs prompt washout with pressure control.
steps.say: Layered blood in the front of the eye after a knock is hyphaema from torn iris or ciliary vessels. The height of the layer guides admission, and sickle trait or disease makes rebleeding catastrophic even when pressure looks low. Management keeps the head up with a shield, dilates with cycloplegics, steadies pressure and watches for the day five rebleed. A black ball of blood or yellow green staining of the cornea needs prompt washout with pressure control.

steps.tx: **Retained intraocular foreign bodies** from hammering metal, farm debris or gunshot pellets localise by CT for metal and by ultrasound or MRI debates for nonmetal. Iron siderosis brings heterochromia, mydriasis, cataract and pigmentary retinopathy with an extinguished electroretinogram, while copper chalcosis gives sunflower cataract with a Kayser Fleischer ring, and both demand prompt vitrectomy removal. Sympathetic ophthalmia can threaten the fellow eye after repair. **Blowout fractures** trap muscle and trigger oculocardiac bradycardia in children needing urgent release, while retrobulbar haemorrhage with tense proptosis needs lateral canthotomy before vision dies.
steps.say: A hammer on metal or a farm injury can leave a fragment inside the eye, so CT hunts metal while ultrasound and MRI debate nonmetal. Iron causes siderosis of the retina and copper causes a corneal ring, and both need prompt vitrectomy removal. The fellow eye stays at risk of sympathetic inflammation after repair. A blowout fracture that traps muscle causes bradycardia in children and needs urgent release, while tense proptosis from retrobulbar bleeding needs lateral canthotomy before vision dies.
